title: Everyone changed
takeaway: When everything around you changes, love is what's left standing.
scene: Things have turned against the poet. His friends have changed, even the seasons seem different, and his love story has become town gossip.

original: جئ بدلی اے تقدیر میری لئے بدل طور سب یاراں نے
پھلاں دی رنگت بدل گئی اجیہا بدلیا رنگ بہاراں نے
transliteration: Jei badli ae taqdeer meri, laye badal taur sab yaaraan ne
Phullaan di rangat badal gayi, ajeha badliya rang bahaaraan ne
translation: As soon as my fate changed, all my friends changed their ways.
Spring changed its colours so much that even the flowers turned a different shade.
couplets.story: The minute his luck turned bad, all his friends started acting differently. Even spring seems to have changed, and the flowers aren't the same colour anymore.

original: کتے دل ہے تے کتے جگر گیا کتے عقل جوانی ہوش گئی
جتھے نین شرابی وار کرن کیہ کرنا اے تلواراں نے
transliteration: Kitte dil hai te kitte jigar gaya, kitte aql jawaani hosh gayi
Jitthe nain sharaabi vaar karan, ki karna ae talwaaraan ne
translation: My heart went one way, my soul another, and my reason, youth and senses somewhere else.
Where intoxicating eyes strike, what use are swords?
couplets.story: He has completely fallen apart. His heart, his soul and his good sense have scattered in different directions. When beautiful eyes attack, swords are useless.

original: پھلاں دی رنگت تک کے تے وچہ مستی خورے کیہ کردا
کنڈیاں نے رولا پا دتا لیا روک مینوں غم خواراں نے
transliteration: Phullaan di rangat tak ke te vich masti khoore ki karda
Kandiyaan ne rola pa ditta, liya rok mainu gham-khaaraan ne
translation: Seeing the colour of the flowers, who knows what I'd have done in my excitement,
but the thorns raised a fuss, and my well-wishers held me back.
couplets.story: He saw the beautiful flowers and almost lost control. The thorns made a fuss, and his friends grabbed him and held him back.

original: میری عشق کہانی پل پل تے اک نواں تماشہ لاندی رہی
وچ جگ دے رسوا کر چھڈیا ہنجواں دی ات قطاراں نے
transliteration: Meri ishq kahaani pal pal te ik navaan tamaasha laandi rahi
Vich jag de ruswa kar chhadiya hanjhuaan di att qataaraan ne
translation: Every moment, my love story put on a new show.
The endless lines of my tears disgraced me in front of the world.
couplets.story: His love life became a show for everyone to watch. His tears kept falling in long lines, and the whole world saw how much he was hurting.

original: کجھ مان نئیں حسباں نسباں دا کوئی ناز نہ حسن جوانی دا
یوسف جیئے اٹی مل پاندے جاو کدے وچہ بزاراں نے
transliteration: Kujh maan nahin hasbaan nasbaan da, koi naaz na husn jawaani da
Yusuf jiye atti mul paande jaave kade vich bazaaraan ne
translation: Don't be proud of your family or your ancestry, or vain about beauty and youth:
even someone like Yusuf was once sold off cheaply in the markets.
couplets.story: Don't be proud of your family name, your good looks or your youth. Even the prophet Yusuf, the most beautiful man ever, was once sold as a slave in a market for a cheap price.

original: او عشق نئیں جو لگ کے تے فیر مرن توں پہلاں مک جاوے
پر ساڈے نال تے لا کے وی سنگ توڑ دتے دلداراں نے
transliteration: O ishq nahin jo lag ke te pher maran ton pehlaan mukk jaave
Par saade naal te la ke vi sang tor ditte dildaaraan ne
translation: Love that takes hold and then runs out before death isn't love.
And yet, with me, the beloved made the bond and then broke it.
couplets.story: Real love doesn't end before you die. If it fades, it wasn't really love. And yet the person he loved made a promise and then broke it.

original: کئی واری توبہ میں کیتی بھن چھڈیا جام صراحیاں نوں
ساقی نوں دیندیاں بھل جاون اے زاہد قول قراراں نے
transliteration: Kayi vaari tauba main keeti, bhann chhadiya jaam suraahiyaan nu
Saaqi nu dendiyaan bhul jaavan, ae zaahid, qaul qaraaraan ne
translation: Many times I repented and smashed the cups and jugs.
But, holy man, the moment I see the saqi, my vows are forgotten.
couplets.story: He tells the strict holy man: I've sworn many times to quit, and even smashed the cups and jugs. But the moment he sees the saqi, every promise goes out of his head.

original: میرے تن تے لیراں لیراں سن میرے سر وچ ٹک مٹی سی
تک جھلیاں دا سردار کہیا مینوں حسن دیاں سرکاراں نے
transliteration: Mere tan te leeraan leeraan san, mere sir vich tikk mitti si
Tak jhalliyaan da sardaar kehiya mainu husn diyaan sarkaaraan ne
translation: My body was in rags and tatters, my head covered in dust;
seeing me, the rulers of beauty named me 'king of the madmen'.
couplets.story: His clothes were in rags and his hair was full of dust. When beauty's royal court saw him like that, they crowned him 'king of the crazy lovers'.

original: ایتھے سنبھل سنبھل کے پیر دھریں ایہہ عشق دی راہ اولڑی اے
ایتھے قدم قدم تے جند واری احمدؔ جیہے کئی ہزاراں نے
transliteration: Ethe sambhal sambhal ke pair dhareen, eh ishq di raah aulri ae
Ethe qadam qadam te jind vaari Ahmad jihe kayi hazaaraan ne
translation: Step carefully here; this road of love is a hard one.
Thousands like Ahmad have given their lives at every step of it.
couplets.story: He ends with a warning. Be careful on the road of love. It's tough. Thousands of people like him have given up their lives at every step along the way.

deeper:
The couplet about Yusuf, sold cheaply in the market, is a story the Qur'an tells at length (chapter 12). Beauty and family status are no protection. Only God's plan lasts. 'Love that ends before death isn't love' is the Sufi standard for devotion to God: lifelong, not a passing phase.

The last couplet is a classic Sufi joke. The poet keeps 'repenting' and breaking the wine cups, but the moment he sees the saqi, the One who pours divine love, every vow is forgotten. The 'wine' he can't give up is love of God, which no rule can stop.
why: It's honest about how friends can change when your luck runs out, and it ends with a smile.
prompt: Who stayed the same with you when your luck changed? What does that tell you about them?
notes: The ghazal continues onto the top of page 53.
